mainTopic: Destroying idols: רבי יוסי's proofs and the חכמים's rejections, איתי הגתי's nullifying, and דוד's crown as a sign of true kingship
overview: The משנה taught that רבי יוסי allows destroying an idol by grinding it up and scattering it. The חכמים worry that the dust could fertilize the ground, which would be forbidden benefit from עבודה זרה. In the ברייתא, רבי יוסי brings four proofs from פסוקים: משה grinding the עגל, אסא burning מעכה's idol at נחל קדרון, חזקיהו crushing the copper snake, and דוד dealing with the פלשתים's idols. The חכמים reject each one. משה was testing the people like a סוטה, נחל קדרון is barren in that spot, the snake was משה's property so it was never forbidden, and דוד's idols were really burned. Two פסוקים about דוד's idols seem to contradict each other, one saying burned and one saying carried away. רב הונא explains that they describe the time before and after איתי הגתי nullified the idols, and the same nullifying explains how דוד could take the crown of מלכם. The גמרא then discusses that crown: how such a heavy crown could sit on his head, and how it fit him as a sign that he was fit to be king. It ends with אדוניה, whom the crown did not fit, and his specially altered runners.

steps.title: Proof from how משה destroyed the golden calf
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי finishes quoting the פסוק in דברים: משה burned and ground the עגל into dust and threw the dust into a stream.
steps.simpleTranslation: …that you made, the calf: I took it, burned it in fire, crushed it and ground it well until it was as fine as dust, and I threw its dust into the stream that comes down from the mountain.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי is finishing his proof from a פסוק. משה ground up the עגל and threw the dust into a stream, which is exactly what רבי יוסי says to do with an idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים worry that ground-up idol dust might fertilize plants, giving forbidden benefit. רבי יוסי points out that משה threw the dust into a stream that could water fields, and he did not seem worried. So, he argues, grinding and scattering is a proper way to destroy an idol.

phrases.english: that you made, the calf
phrases.notes: This is the end of a פסוק that רבי יוסי started quoting just before: דברים 9:21.

phrases.english: I took, and I burned it in fire
and I crushed it, grinding it well
until it was fine as dust
and I threw its dust
into the stream that comes down from the mountain!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי יוסי's proof, which began just before this section
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי's view that grinding an idol and scattering it is enough, even though the dust could fertilize
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 9:21, where משה ground the עגל and threw it into a stream

steps.title: Rejection: משה was testing the people like a סוטה
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that משה scattered the dust on the water so the people would drink it, as a test like the waters of a סוטה. He was not using it as a normal way to destroy an idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: You bring a proof from there? But the פסוק says, 'He scattered it on the water and made the children of Israel drink.' He only meant to test them, like women suspected of being unfaithful.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי יוסי's proof. They say משה's case was special: he had a different purpose for the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Another פסוק, in שמות, shows that משה made the people drink the water with the dust in it. That means his goal was to test who had sinned, the way a סוטה is tested by drinking. So his case teaches nothing about the usual way to destroy an idol.

keyTerms.meaning: "You bring a proof from there?", a phrase used to reject a proof
Women suspected by their husbands of being unfaithful, who are tested by drinking special water

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים are not saying משה did something wrong. They are saying his act had a special purpose, testing the people, so it cannot be used to learn the normal rule.

phrases.english: They said to him: You bring a proof from there?
But look, it says:
"And he scattered it on the surface of the water
phrases.notes: שמות 32:20

phrases.english: and made the children of Israel drink"
he intended nothing other than
to test them, like sotah women.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from משה and the עגל
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the עגל, not רבי יוסי's view itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: משה's purpose was to test the people, not simply to destroy the idol, so his case is a special one

steps.title: Second proof: אסא burned his mother's idol at נחל קדרון
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי brings another פסוק: אסא crushed and burned his mother מעכה's idol at נחל קדרון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said to them: But it already says, 'And also מעכה his mother he removed from being queen, because she made a disgusting idol… and he crushed it and burned it at נחל קדרון!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי tries again with a new proof. This time there is no drinking or testing, just an idol being destroyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אסא crushed the idol and burned it at a riverbed, where the ashes could end up fertilizing the ground. This case has no special purpose like משה's, so רבי יוסי says it shows that destroying an idol this way is acceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: "But hasn't it already been said…", introducing a proof from a פסוק

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said to them:
But hasn't it already been said
"And also Maacah his mother
he removed her from being queen
because she made a disgusting image, etc.
and he crushed it and burned it at the Kidron stream!"

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After his first proof is rejected, רבי יוסי brings a second one
steps.raayaObject: Grinding an idol and leaving it where it could fertilize is acceptable
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק about אסא destroying מעכה's idol at נחל קדרון

steps.title: Rejection: נחל קדרון grows nothing
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that נחל קדרון does not grow plants, so the ashes there could never become useful fertilizer.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: You bring a proof from there? נחל קדרון does not grow plants!
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים reject רבי יוסי's second proof too. They say the place אסא chose was barren.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים's concern is that the dust might help plants grow, which would be benefit from עבודה זרה. If nothing grows at נחל קדרון, there is no benefit, so אסא's act does not prove that grinding is fine in a normal place.

phrases.english: He said to him: You bring a proof from there?
The Kidron stream does not grow plants!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from אסא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: נחל קדרון is barren, so no benefit could come from the dust there

steps.title: Challenge: the מקדש blood was sold as fertilizer at קדרון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that נחל קדרון grows nothing. A משנה says the leftover blood from the מקדש flowed to נחל קדרון and was sold to gardeners as fertilizer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does it really not grow plants? But we learned: these and those mix together in the channel, flow out to נחל קדרון, are sold to gardeners as fertilizer, and one who uses them without paying commits מעילה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא itself steps in to question what the חכמים said about נחל קדרון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If gardeners paid for the blood at נחל קדרון to fertilize their gardens, then plants must grow there. This seems to cancel the חכמים's rejection of רבי יוסי's proof.

keyTerms.meaning: A water channel (here, in the עזרה of the מקדש)
They commit מעילה, misusing holy property

phrases.english: And does it not? But wasn't it taught:
these and those mix together in the channel,
phrases.notes: "These and those" means the leftover blood from the two מזבחות in the מקדש.

phrases.english: and they flow out to the Kidron stream,
and are sold to gardeners for fertilizer,
and one commits me'ilah with them!
phrases.notes: Me'ilah is the sin of using holy property for yourself, so this means the blood is still holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the factual claim in the rejection just given
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's claim that נחל קדרון does not grow plants
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה says the blood at נחל קדרון was sold to gardeners as fertilizer, which only makes sense if plants grow there

steps.title: Answer: קדרון has fertile spots and barren spots
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that נחל קדרון is not all the same. Some parts grow plants and some do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are different places in it: there is a place that grows plants, and there is a place that does not grow plants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying both sources are true, each about a different part of נחל קדרון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gardeners used the blood in the fertile parts, while אסא burned the idol in a barren part. So the חכמים's rejection of רבי יוסי's proof still stands.
steps.whatToRemember: Both of רבי יוסי's proofs are pushed aside. משה was testing the people like a סוטה, and אסא burned the idol in a barren part of נחל קדרון. The חכמים's concern about the dust giving benefit as fertilizer remains.

phrases.english: There are different places in it:
there is a place that grows plants,
and there is a place that does not grow plants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge and defends the חכמים's rejection
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the location: the two sources are about different parts of נחל קדרון
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נחל קדרון seemed to be fertile everywhere, since gardeners bought fertilizer there
steps.terutzMaskana: Parts of נחל קדרון are fertile and parts are barren; אסא used a barren part

steps.title: What does the word מִפְלַצְתָּהּ mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pauses to ask what the word מִפְלַצְתָּהּ means. This is the word the פסוק uses for מעכה's idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'מִפְלַצְתָּהּ'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes a short side trip to ask about a hard word in the פסוק about אסא and מעכה. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This question does not attack anyone's argument. It is a plain word question about the פסוק quoted in Step 3. The main debate between רבי יוסי and the חכמים pauses for a moment.

keyTerms.meaning: What? (asking for the meaning of something)
Her 'מפלצת', the word the פסוק uses for מעכה's idol

phrases.english: What is 'miflatztah'?
phrases.notes: This is the word from the פסוק about אסא and his mother מעכה in Step 3 (מלכים א 15:13).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side question about a word in the פסוק from Step 3, asked after the קשיא and תירוץ about נחל קדרון are finished.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word מִפְלַצְתָּהּ in the פסוק about מעכה's idol.

steps.title: An idol that increased immorality
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that מִפְלַצְתָּהּ means something that 'greatly increased immorality'. He supports this with רב יוסף's teaching that מעכה made the idol in an immoral shape and used it in an immoral way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: It was something that greatly increased immorality. This matches what רב יוסף taught: she made for herself something shaped like a male organ, and she used it immorally every day.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the word question. He explains the word מִפְלַצְתָּהּ by splitting it into two parts: 'מפליא' (makes great) and 'ליצנותא' (immorality).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word is read as a mix of two ideas: something that 'makes great' (מַפְלְיָא) the 'immorality' (לֵיצָנוּתָא). רב יוסף's teaching shows what this looked like in real life. This finishes the side trip, and the גמרא then goes back to quoting the ברייתא's debate.

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught (bringing support from a ברייתא teaching)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
It was something that greatly increased immorality,
phrases.notes: He's reading מִפְלַצְתָּהּ as two words joined together: מַפְלְיָא and לֵיצָנוּתָא.

phrases.english: as Rav Yosef taught:
she made for herself a kind of male organ,
and she would be intimate with it every day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: דַּהֲוָה מַפְלְיָא לֵיצָנוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the word question asked in Step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מִפְלַצְתָּהּ means an object that increased immorality. רב יוסף's teaching about its immoral shape and use supports this.

steps.title: A new proof: חזקיהו crushed משה's copper snake
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי brings another proof that crushing an idol is enough. The פסוק says that King חזקיהו crushed the copper snake that משה made, which people had been worshipping.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said to them: But isn't it already written, 'And he crushed the copper snake that משה had made'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes back to the main debate. רבי יוסי tries a third proof that grinding up an idol is a proper way to destroy it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people had been bringing offerings to the copper snake, so it looks like an idol. The פסוק says it was crushed, not burned or thrown into the sea. So רבי יוסי argues that crushing is enough to destroy an idol.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it already written? (a way of opening a proof from a פסוק)
And he crushed or broke into pieces
The copper snake that משה made in the desert

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said to them,
but isn't it already stated:
'And he crushed the copper snake
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 18:4. 'He' is King חזקיהו.

phrases.english: that Moshe had made'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the נחל קדרון discussion and the word explanation, רבי יוסי brings a new proof to replace the one the חכמים pushed away.
steps.raayaObject: Crushing an idol into pieces is a proper way to destroy it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים ב 18:4. חזקיהו crushed the copper snake that משה made, which people had worshipped.

steps.title: The snake belonged to משה, so it was never forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject the proof. ה׳ told משה 'make for yourself', so the snake belonged to משה. A person cannot make forbidden something that is not his, so the snake never became a forbidden idol and did not legally need to be destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: You bring a proof from there? The פסוק says, 'And ה׳ said to משה: Make for yourself a snake.' 'For yourself' means from your own property. A person cannot make forbidden something that is not his. So in that case, by law, it did not even need to be crushed.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים say the snake is not a good proof. It was never a forbidden idol in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The snake belonged to משה. When the people later worshipped it, they could not make it forbidden, because a person can only make his own things forbidden. So the case says nothing about how to destroy a real idol, since there was no real idol here to destroy.

keyTerms.meaning: You bring a proof from there? (pushing a proof away)
A fiery snake (the snake משה was told to make)

keyTerms.term: אֵין אָדָם אוֹסֵר דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: A person cannot make forbidden something that does not belong to him
By law; according to the strict rule

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים are not saying that worshipping the snake was allowed. They are saying it never got the legal status of a forbidden idol, because the worshippers did not own it.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'אין אדם אוסר דבר שאינו שלו' is a basic rule in the laws of עבודה זרה. Worshipping someone else's object does not make that object forbidden.

phrases.english: They said to him: Is there a proof from there?
Look, it says:
'And ה׳ said to Moshe,
phrases.notes: במדבר 21:8

phrases.english: make for yourself a fiery snake,'
'for yourself' means from your own property,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין אָדָם אוֹסֵר דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ,
phrases.english: and a person does not make forbidden something that is not his,
phrases.notes: The people who worshipped the snake did not own it, so their worship could not make it forbidden.

phrases.english: and there, by law,
it did not need to be crushed at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יוסי's proof from the copper snake in Step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the copper snake. It does not teach anything about how to destroy a real idol.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The snake belonged to משה, so the people who worshipped it could not make it forbidden. It was never a legal idol that needed destroying.

steps.title: Why חזקיהו crushed it anyway
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים explain that חזקיהו crushed the snake only because he saw people being led astray by it. He was not doing the מצוה of destroying an idol, so crushing it was enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, once he saw that the Jewish people were going astray after it, he got up and crushed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים answer the obvious follow-up question: if the snake did not need to be destroyed, why did חזקיהו crush it? He did it to stop people from worshipping it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Crushing the snake was a practical step to stop people from going astray. It was not the formal מצוה of getting rid of עבודה זרה. That is why crushing it, instead of using a stronger method, tells us nothing about how a real idol must be destroyed.

keyTerms.meaning: He got up and crushed it

steps.whatToRemember: The copper snake is no proof for רבי יוסי. It was משה's property, so it was never truly forbidden. חזקיהו crushed it only to stop people from going astray.

phrases.english: Rather, since he saw
phrases.notes: 'He' is King חזקיהו, from the פסוק רבי יוסי quoted.

phrases.english: that the Jewish people were going astray after it,
he got up and crushed it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, כֵּיוָן דַּחֲזָא דְּקָא טָעוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּתְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the חכמים's rejection by explaining why חזקיהו crushed a snake that did not legally need to be destroyed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the reason behind the action: it was done to stop people from going astray, not to fulfill the מצוה of destroying an idol.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the snake did not need destroying, why does the פסוק say חזקיהו crushed it?
steps.terutzMaskana: He crushed it as a practical step against people going astray. So crushing it teaches nothing about how to properly destroy a real idol.

steps.title: רבי יוסי brings the פסוק about דוד and the פלשתים's idols
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי brings his fourth proof, after the עגל, אסא's idol and the copper snake. The פסוק says that דוד and his men did וַיִּשָּׂאֵם to the idols the פלשתים left behind.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Isn't it already stated: 'And they left their idols there, and דוד and his men וַיִּשָּׂאֵם them'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי brings another פסוק to prove that you can get rid of an idol without burning it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His last proof, the copper snake, was rejected because the snake was never a real idol. So he now brings a case of real idols: the פלשתים's gods. If דוד disposed of them in a way other than burning, that would support רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: The key word. It can mean 'he carried them away' or 'he scattered them in the wind'

phrases.english: He said to them,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוסי answering the חכמים.

phrases.english: But isn't it already stated:
'And they left their idols there,'
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 5:21

phrases.english: 'and David and his men vayyissa'em them.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After his snake proof was pushed off, רבי יוסי brings a new proof.
steps.raayaObject: That getting rid of an idol by a method other than burning is enough

steps.title: How do we know the word means scattering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that וַיִּשָּׂאֵם means scattering in the wind.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that this word 'וַיִּשָּׂאֵם דוד' is a word for winnowing, meaning scattering in the wind?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask why we should read וַיִּשָּׂאֵם as 'scattered' rather than just 'carried.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's proof only works if the word means scattering, which is a way of destroying. If it only means 'carried away,' the פסוק says nothing about how the idols were destroyed.

keyTerms.meaning: How do we know? What shows that?
A word that means winnowing, scattering in the wind

phrases.english: And from where may it be inferred that this 'vayyissa'em David'
is a term for winnowing?
phrases.notes: Winnowing means tossing something into the wind so it blows away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the key word in רבי יוסי's proof means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What shows that וַיִּשָּׂאֵם means scattering in the wind

steps.title: רב יוסף's translation shows the word means scattering
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף's Aramaic translation of a פסוק in ישעיה shows that תִּשָּׂאֵם means the wind blowing things away.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יוסף translates: 'You shall winnow them, and the wind shall תִּשָּׂאֵם them.' And we translate it: 'You shall winnow them, and the wind shall carry them off.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by showing that the same word is used in ישעיה for the wind scattering things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ישעיה, תִּשָּׂאֵם is paired with winnowing and the wind. The translation turns it into 'the wind will carry them off.' So וַיִּשָּׂאֵם by דוד can also mean scattering, and that supports רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: You shall winnow them, toss them into the wind
We translate it into Aramaic as
Will carry them off, move them away

phrases.english: As Rav Yosef translates:
'You shall winnow them, and the wind shall tissa'em them,'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 41:16

phrases.english: and we translate it:
'You shall winnow them, and the wind shall carry them off.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the meaning of the word.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The same word in ישעיה 41:16 means the wind scattering things, so וַיִּשָּׂאֵם can mean scattering.

steps.title: The חכמים show the idols were burned, so the word just means carried
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject the proof. The parallel פסוק in דברי הימים says the idols were burned. So וַיִּשָּׂאֵם simply means 'they carried them away.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Is that a proof? It says 'and they were burned in fire.' And since it does not say 'he burned them and scattered them,' learn from this that וַיִּשָּׂאֵם means literally carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push off רבי יוסי's proof. They point to another פסוק that says דוד's idols were burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the idols were really scattered, the פסוק could have written 'he burned them and scattered them.' Since it only says they were burned, the burning is how they were destroyed. וַיִּשָּׂאֵם just means picking them up and carrying them off. So this פסוק is no proof that scattering alone is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that a proof? You want to prove it from there?
And they were burned in fire

phrases.english: They said to him: Is there proof from there?
It says, 'and they were burned in fire,'
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 14:12. It tells the same story about דוד.

phrases.english: and since it is not written 'and he burned them and vayyissa'em them,'
learn from it that 'vayyissa'em' is literal.
phrases.notes: They mean he simply picked them up and carried them off. It does not mean scattering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יוסי's fourth proof, the one from דוד and the פלשתים's idols.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from דוד and the פלשתים's idols
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The parallel פסוק shows the idols were burned, so וַיִּשָּׂאֵם means carrying, not scattering.
steps.whatToRemember: All four of רבי יוסי's proofs (משה and the עגל, אסא at נחל קדרון, the copper snake, and דוד's idols) are pushed off by the חכמים.

steps.title: Still, the two verses contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: Either way, the גמרא notes that the two פסוקים seem to contradict each other. One says carried or scattered, and the other says burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the verses contradict each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem no matter how we read the word. The two accounts of the same story do not match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל says דוד and his men did וַיִּשָּׂאֵם to the idols. דברי הימים says they were burned. These describe the same event, so we need to explain how both can be true.

phrases.english: In any case,
the verses contradict each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the argument between רבי יוסי and the חכמים to a contradiction between the פסוקים themselves.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two פסוקים: שמואל ב 5:21 and דברי הימים א 14:12
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק says the idols were carried away or scattered, and the other says they were burned. These are two different accounts of the same event.

steps.title: The answer follows רב הונא, who raised this same contradiction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the answer follows רב הונא. It first quotes רב הונא's question: one פסוק says 'burned' and the other says 'וַיִּשָּׂאֵם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like רב הונא, since רב הונא pointed out a contradiction: It is written 'And דוד said, and they were burned in fire,' and it is written 'וַיִּשָּׂאֵם'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its answer. It points to רב הונא, who asked this same question, and quotes his question first. His actual answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not invent a new answer. It shows that רב הונא already raised this contradiction and solved it. Here we only hear the setup of his question. The resolution follows right after.

keyTerms.meaning: Points out a contradiction between two sources
It is written... and it is written. This sets two פסוקים against each other

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the answer has already been given here. This step only quotes רב הונא's question. His answer comes in the next lines.

phrases.english: In accordance with Rav Huna,
as Rav Huna raises a contradiction:
It is written, 'And David said, and they were burned in fire,'
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 14:12

phrases.english: and it is written, 'vayyissa'em'!
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 5:21

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the contradiction by pointing to רב הונא, who asked the same question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Referral to an earlier אמורא's resolution of the same contradiction. The resolution itself comes next.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים give conflicting accounts of how דוד disposed of the idols.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב הונא already dealt with this exact contradiction, and his resolution will explain it.

steps.title: Before and after איתי arrived
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the 'burned' פסוק describes the time before איתי הגתי came, and the 'carried away' פסוק describes the time after he came.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. One פסוק is talking about the time before איתי הגתי came, and the other is talking about the time after איתי הגתי came.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא solves the contradiction between the two פסוקים by saying they describe two different points in time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first the idols still had the status of עבודה זרה, so they had to be burned. Once איתי הגתי, a non-Jew, came and nullified them (ביטול), they were no longer forbidden, so they could simply be carried away. Both פסוקים are true, just at different moments.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the opening words of an answer
Ittai from Gath, a non-Jew who joined דוד

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say these were different idols. They may be the same idols at two different times; what changed is whether איתי had already nullified them.

phrases.english: It is not difficult.
Here, it was before Ittai the Gittite came,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the פסוק that says the idols were burned.

phrases.english: there, it was after Ittai the Gittite came.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן — קוֹדֶם שֶׁבָּא אִיתַּי הַגִּיתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב הונא's answer, which was set up in step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two time periods: before and after nullification
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוקים contradict each other: burned vs. carried away
steps.terutzMaskana: Burned before איתי nullified them; carried away after

steps.title: How could דוד use the idol's crown?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another פסוק: דוד took the crown off the idol מלכם. It asks how that was allowed, since an idol's items are forbidden for any benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And he took the crown of Malcam from off his head, and its weight was a talent of gold.' But is that allowed? These are things you may not benefit from!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem about דוד, and איתי הגתי will solve this one too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anything used for עבודה זרה is אסור בהנאה, meaning no benefit may be taken from it. Yet the פסוק says דוד took the crown and used it. So how was this allowed?

keyTerms.meaning: A talent of gold, a very heavy weight
Things you may not benefit from in any way

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And he took the crown of Malcam
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 12:30. The פסוק goes on to say the crown was placed on דוד's head.

phrases.english: from off his head,
and its weight was a talent of gold."
But is it permitted?
They are items forbidden for benefit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second case that the arrival of איתי will also explain
steps.kashyaTarget: דוד's use of the crown of מלכם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Items of עבודה זרה are אסור בהנאה, so דוד could not wear the crown

steps.title: איתי nullified the crown
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that איתי הגתי came and nullified the crown, so it was no longer forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: איתי הגתי came and nullified it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the question: the crown was permitted because איתי nullified it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once an idol or its ornament is properly nullified, it stops being forbidden. So the same arrival of איתי that explains the idols being carried away also explains how דוד could use the crown.

keyTerms.meaning: He nullified it, removing its status as an idol
Nullifying an idol so it becomes permitted

steps.whatToRemember: The arrival of איתי הגתי, who nullified the idols, explains two things: why the idols were later carried away instead of burned, and how דוד could wear the crown of מלכם.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman says:
Ittai the Gittite came and nullified it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: אִיתַּי הַגִּיתִּי בָּא וּבִיטְּלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 19
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The crown was still forbidden for benefit
steps.terutzMaskana: איתי nullified it, so דוד could use it

steps.title: How could דוד wear such a heavy crown?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how דוד could wear a crown that weighed a whole talent of gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Its weight was a talent of gold. How could he put it on?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new question about the same crown: it was far too heavy to wear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A talent is a huge weight, much too heavy for a person to wear on his head. Yet the פסוק says the crown was placed on דוד's head, so the גמרא asks how that worked. Three answers follow.

keyTerms.meaning: How could he? / How is it possible?

phrases.english: Its weight was a talent of gold;
how could he place it on his head?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשְׁקָלָהּ כִּכַּר זָהָב, הֵיכִי מָצֵי מַנַּח לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question about the same פסוק
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How a crown weighing a talent of gold could rest on דוד's head

steps.title: It was fit for דוד's head
steps.stepSummary: רב says the פסוק only means the crown fit דוד's head, not that he actually wore it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: It was fit to rest on דוד's head.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first answer: דוד did not actually wear it; the פסוק just means it was the right size for his head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'it was on דוד's head' are read as describing the crown's fit, not that he carried its weight. That removes the problem.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says that Rav says:
It was fit to rest on David's head.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: רְאוּיָה לָנוּחַ עַל רֹאשׁ דָּוִד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He did not really wear it; it simply fit his head

steps.title: A magnet held it up
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says a magnetic stone held the crown up, so its weight did not rest on דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: There was a lodestone in it that held it up.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second answer: the crown was held up by a magnet, so דוד did not carry its weight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this view the crown really was on דוד's head, but a lodestone kept it lifted. So he could wear it without being crushed by it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, says:
There was a lodestone in it,
which would hold it up.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: אֶבֶן שׁוֹאֶבֶת הָיְתָה בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second answer to step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A lodestone held the crown up

steps.title: It was worth a talent of gold
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the crown did not weigh a talent; it had a precious stone worth a talent of gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: There was a precious stone in it that was worth a talent of gold.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a third answer: the פסוק is talking about the crown's value, not its weight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר reads 'a talent of gold' as describing how much a gem in it was worth. The crown itself could be light enough to wear normally.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
There was a precious stone in it
that was worth a talent of gold.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר: אֶבֶן יְקָרָה הָיְתָה בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third answer to step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The talent is its value, not its weight

steps.title: What does 'This I have had' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק in תהלים and asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'This I have had, because I kept Your commandments.' What is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק spoken by דוד and asks what 'this' refers to. It is setting up a link back to the crown.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'this' was given to דוד, but it does not say what 'this' is. The גמרא wants to explain the vague word.

phrases.english: "This I have had,
phrases.notes: תהלים 119:56

phrases.english: because I kept Your precepts":
What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question about a related פסוק
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What 'this' refers to in the פסוק

steps.title: The crown was a testimony
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains: as a reward for keeping the מצוות, 'this' (the crown) was a testimony for דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it is saying: As a reward for keeping Your commandments, this was a testimony for me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the פסוק: 'this' is the crown, and it served as a sign for דוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The crown was a reward and a proof that דוד was fit to be king. The גמרא will next ask what exactly this sign was.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is saying

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
As reward for keeping Your precepts,
this was a testimony for me.
phrases.notes: 'This' is the crown, a sign that דוד was fit to be king.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The crown was a reward and a testimony for דוד

steps.title: What was the testimony?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in what way the crown was a testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was its testimony?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question: how did the crown prove anything about דוד?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying the crown was a 'testimony' is still vague. The גמרא wants to know what exactly it showed.

phrases.english: What was its testimony?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follow-up to step 26
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what way the crown testified for דוד

steps.title: It fit exactly where תפילין go
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says דוד would put the crown on the spot of the תפילין, and it fit him perfectly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: He would place it on the spot of the תפילין, and it fit him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי answers that the crown's perfect fit on the spot of the תפילין was the sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The crown fit דוד's head exactly in the place where תפילין are worn. That perfect fit showed he was fit to be king.

keyTerms.meaning: On the spot where תפילין are worn

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says:
That he would place it on the spot of the phylacteries,
and it fit him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: שֶׁהָיָה מַנִּיחָהּ בִּמְקוֹם תְּפִילִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 27
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The crown fit perfectly on the spot of the תפילין

steps.title: But he had to wear תפילין there
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if the crown sat where the תפילין go, where did דוד put his תפילין?
steps.simpleTranslation: But he needed to put on תפילין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהושע בן לוי's answer: the crown would take up the place of the תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד was obligated to wear תפילין on that same spot. If the crown was there, it seems he could not fulfill the מצוה.

phrases.english: But he needed to don phylacteries!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 28
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's claim that the crown sat on the spot of the תפילין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The crown would block the spot where דוד had to wear תפילין

steps.title: There is room for two תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק answers that the spot for תפילין on the head is big enough for two, so there was room for both the crown and the תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק said: There is a place on the head big enough to put two תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק answers the challenge: there is enough room for both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The area on the head where תפילין may be worn is wide enough for two. So דוד could wear the crown and his תפילין together.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a place on the head

steps.whatToRemember: The crown fit דוד perfectly on the spot of the תפילין as a sign that he was fit to be king. There was still room for his תפילין, because that area can hold two.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzḥak says:
There is a place on the head
that is fit for donning two phylacteries.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק: מָקוֹם יֵשׁ בָּרֹאשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 29
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The crown takes up the only place for the תפילין
steps.terutzMaskana: The area holds two, so both fit

steps.title: The פסוק about יואש: crown and testimony
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק describing how יואש was crowned with the נזר and the עדות, and explains that נזר means the crown.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they brought out the king's son, and put upon him the crown and the testimony.' 'Crown' means the royal crown.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new פסוק about a crown, from the crowning of young יואש. It explains the first word, נזר, and sets up a question about the second word, עדות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the topic of a crown that 'testifies' about the king, as in the case of דוד in the earlier steps. The word נזר is easy: it is the crown. The harder word, עדות, is explained in the next step.

phrases.english: "And they brought out the king's son,
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 23:11, about the crowning of יואש.

phrases.aramaic: וַיִּתְּנוּ עָלָיו אֶת הַנֵּזֶר וְאֶת הָעֵדוּת״,
phrases.english: and put upon him the crown and the testimony."
"Nezer" is a crown.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיּוֹצִיאוּ אֶת בֶּן הַמֶּלֶךְ וַיִּתְּנוּ עָלָיו אֶת הַנֵּזֶר וְאֶת הָעֵדוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another פסוק that ties the royal crown to the idea of 'testimony', continuing the discussion of דוד's crown.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the פסוק about יואש, נזר means the royal crown.

steps.title: The crown fits only someone fit to be king
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that the 'testimony' is that the crown fits a member of בית דוד who is fit for kingship and does not fit one who is unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the 'testimony'? רב יהודה said in the name of רב: it is a testimony for בית דוד. Whoever is fit to be king, the crown fits him. Whoever is not fit to be king, the crown does not fit him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains the word עדות in the פסוק. The crown itself acts as a sign showing who in בית דוד is really fit to be king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא said the crown fit דוד perfectly. Here רב turns that into a general rule for the whole family: the crown is a natural test. If it fits, the person is fit for מלכות; if not, he is not.

keyTerms.meaning: The family of דוד, the royal line

steps.whatToRemember: The crown of בית דוד works as a test: it fits only the one who is truly fit to rule.

phrases.english: "Testimony":
Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
It is a testimony for the house of David,
that anyone who is fit for kingship, it fits him,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the crown.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינוֹ רָאוּי לַמַּלְכוּת אֵין הוֹלַמְתּוֹ.
phrases.english: and anyone who is not fit for kingship, it does not fit him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: עֵדוּת הוּא לְבֵית דָּוִד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second word of the פסוק quoted in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The crown of בית דוד fits only someone fit for kingship.

steps.title: אדוניה tried to make the crown fit him
steps.stepSummary: רב reads the word מתנשא in the פסוק about אדוניה as meaning that he tried to make the crown fit him, but it did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And אדוניה son of חגית exalted himself, saying: I will be king.' רב יהודה said in the name of רב: he tried to make the crown fit him, but it did not fit him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the crown test to אדוניה, the son of דוד who tried to take the throne. Since he was not the chosen king, the crown did not fit him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מתנשא literally means 'lifting himself up'. רב reads it as a hint to the crown test from the previous step. אדוניה tried to become king, but the crown showed he was not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: אדוניה, a son of דוד who tried to seize the throne

phrases.english: "Now Adonijah son of Haggith exalted himself,
phrases.notes: מלכים א 1:5.

phrases.english: saying: I will be king."
Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
That he tried to make it fit him, and it did not fit him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲדֹנִיָּה בֶן חַגִּית מִתְנַשֵּׂא לֵאמֹר אֲנִי אֶמְלֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the crown test from the previous step to a case where someone failed it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אדוניה tried to make the crown fit him, and it did not, showing he was not fit to be king.

steps.title: What was special about אדוניה's runners?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the rest of the פסוק about אדוניה's chariots and fifty runners and asks what was unusual about them.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he prepared for himself chariots and riders and fifty men to run before him.' What was special about them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the same פסוק and asks a question. It sets up the next step, which will give the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any rich person could have chariots and runners, so why does the פסוק bother to mention them? The גמרא assumes the פסוק is telling us something unusual about these runners.

phrases.english: "And he prepared for himself chariots and riders,
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, מלכים א 1:5.

phrases.english: and fifty men to run before him."
What is the novelty of them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next words of the same פסוק about אדוניה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What was unusual about אדוניה's fifty runners that the פסוק mentions them.

steps.title: The runners were specially altered to run fast
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that all of אדוניה's runners had their spleens removed and the soles of their feet cut out.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: all of them had their spleens removed and the soles of their feet hollowed out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא. The runners were not ordinary; their bodies had been changed so they could run faster.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing the spleen and cutting flesh from the soles of the feet were thought to make a person a faster runner. This is the unusual detail that makes the פסוק worth mentioning, and it shows how hard אדוניה worked to look like a king.

keyTerms.meaning: With the soles of their feet hollowed out

steps.whatToRemember: אדוניה tried hard to act like a king, with crown and special runners, but the crown showed he was not fit.

phrases.english: It was taught:
All of them had their spleens removed
and had the soles of their feet hollowed out.
phrases.notes: Flesh was cut from their soles; both changes were meant to make them run faster.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The runners all had their spleens removed and the soles of their feet hollowed, which made them unusually fast.
